reason: Re-examined transitive proof route after the finite corner-sector construction was made explicit for reflex as well as convex ordinary corners. Full Lee Chapter 9, Datar Lectures 1–2, Jost §2.3.A and Wendl §6.3 were inspected; current direct prerequisites are listed in dependencies. Proof strategy: Following Lee Problem 9-5 and Jost §2.3.A, choose a finite r-net and inside each convex 3r-ball a small geodesic polygon containing a covering r-ball. Perturb finite interior vertices before joining by unique short geodesics; exclude coincident edges and nontransverse crossings. Distinct smooth geodesic arcs can meet only transversely unless local ODE uniqueness forces overlap, so compactness gives finitely many crossings per pair. Insert crossing vertices and overlay covering polygon boundaries. Membership in a covering polygon is constant on each face, so every face lies in a selected convex chart. Apply the local planar graph disk-cut lemma to split holes and remaining faces into disks. Along smooth boundary arcs, use a finite collar net, short inward cross-arcs and prescribed boundary arcs before adding an inner polygonal network. At each ordinary corner, anchor it as a vertex and subdivide its interior tangent sector into finitely many directions with successive gaps less than π/2; this also handles reflex corners. Choose nearby points on those rays, join consecutive rays by short geodesic arcs and join the outermost sectors to adjacent boundary collar cells. In a sufficiently small chart the strict angular margins and smooth dependence of short geodesics keep every new arc inside the domain. This supplies the corner variant locally without pretending a general collar theorem applies at the corner.
